record.paper_title: Progresses on some open problems related to infinitely many symmetries
record.original_question: Can generalized symmetries, especially generalized local symmetries rather than only Lie point symmetries or nonlocal symmetry constraints, be used to derive exact multi-wave solutions of integrable partial differential equation systems, in particular multi-soliton solutions and other exact solutions beyond single periodic cnoidal waves, solitary waves, and Painlevé-type solutions?

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 3: Finding multi-wave solutions via generalized symmetries
While symmetries and conservation laws are instrumental in deriving general solutions for integrable ODE systems, the analogous application within the context of integrable PDEs presents a significant challenge. Despite the fact that several Lie point symmetries have been successfully applied to identify single periodic cnoidal wave solutions, including solitary waves, and Painlevé solutions, the utilization of the vast array of general symmetries to find exact solutions in PDE systems is an unresolved issue.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let an integrable system of partial differential equations be given, admitting an infinite hierarchy of generalized symmetries (in the sense of Olver), i.e., evolutionary vector fields whose characteristics depend on the dependent variables and finitely many of their derivatives. Such systems also typically admit a finite-dimensional Lie point symmetry algebra (whose invariant reductions are known to yield single-phase exact solutions such as solitary waves, single periodic cnoidal waves, and Painlevé-type self-similar reductions) as well as nonlocal symmetries (e.g., from potential or pseudopotential constructions).

Develop a systematic method that uses genuine generalized (higher-order, local) symmetries — rather than only Lie point symmetries or nonlocal symmetry constraints — to construct exact multi-wave solutions of the system. In particular:

1. Show whether invariance under suitable combinations of generalized local symmetries (or finite linear combinations of higher-order symmetry flows) can be used to characterize and explicitly construct N-soliton solutions for N ≥ 2.

2. Determine whether such generalized-symmetry reductions can produce multi-phase (quasi-periodic) wave solutions, including finite-gap / algebro-geometric solutions, going beyond single periodic cnoidal waves, solitary waves, and Painlevé-type reductions.

3. Provide either a general construction valid for a class of integrable PDEs (such as the KdV, modified KdV, sine-Gordon, or nonlinear Schrödinger hierarchies) or a proof of obstruction explaining why generalized local symmetries alone cannot yield multi-wave exact solutions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicitly open problem in current literature on symmetries of integrable PDEs. While Lie point and nonlocal symmetries have produced single-phase exact solutions, no general method using generalized local symmetries to derive multi-soliton or multi-phase exact solutions is established. No definitive resolution was found.
